function: Deep reinforcement learning jointly sets bits per semantic symbol, passive IRS reflective coefficients and OFDMA subchannel assignment to maximize secure semantic spectrum efficiency (pp. 1, 5-6).
system: OFDMA downlink, 3-antenna transmitter, three single-antenna users, one single-antenna eavesdropper, passive reflecting IRS with 64 elements (16-512), three 90 kHz subchannels, no carrier stated (pp. 4, 10).
method: Hybrid DRL: NoisyNet-Dueling DQN for bits and subchannels, NoisyNet-SAC for IRS coefficients, semantic-context-aware state; VQ-VAE semantic codec pre-trained, then fine-tuned jointly (pp. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulated channels: Rician for transmitter-IRS and IRS-users links, Rayleigh for direct links, distance path loss; images from PASCAL VOC-2007 and ImageNet (p. 10).
test_conditions: Codec trained at 10 dB SNR, validated at -10 to 15 dB (p. 11); DRL swept over noise variance and IRS size 16-512 (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: AO Traditional Method (40 iterations) [17], no-IRS scheme; learned: conventional HDRL [16], NdeHDRL-DT with TD3; codec: CNN-AE, JPEG2000/BPG plus Turbo; PL-SS [12], AL-SS [8] (pp. 10-13).
metrics: Semantic similarity (SSIM minus LPIPS), semantic security performance, secure semantic spectrum efficiency (S-SSE), reward, CPU execution time (pp. 5, 11-13).
complexity: Measured CPU time (Table IV): 14.64 ms for the proposed scheme versus 512.34 to 1231.67 ms for AO with 20 to 60 iterations (p. 13).
openness: none; no code or data link, only public image datasets PASCAL VOC-2007 and ImageNet are used (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 10: "The channels from the transmitter to the IRS and from the IRS to the users follow Rician fading models, and the channels from the transmitter to the users follow Rayleigh fading models"; custom simulator, with no 3GPP model, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "the validity of our adopted semantic coding network with several benchmark schemes versus different SNR on the validation dataset"; only sweeps over SNR, noise variance and IRS elements are reported, with no unseen channel, layout, user or dataset tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "we compare the conventional HDRL scheme [16] and the CSO-SS scheme"; p. 10: "the Traditional Method scheme using AO algorithm with 40 iterations [17] is introduced"; p. 12: "our proposed NdeHDRL method can achieve 15.4% semantic security improvement compared to the HDRL-DS scheme"; p. 13: "our proposed scheme can outperform the Traditional Method scheme"
q4_support: p. 13: "we assess computational efficiency and perform latency analysis by measuring the average execution time of the algorithms on central processing units (CPUs)"; p. 13: "our proposed scheme is over 60 times more efficient in terms of execution time compared to the Traditional Method scheme"
q5_support: p. 10: "The Database is set as PASCAL VOC-2007 and ImageNet"; these are image datasets of the learning task only, the channels are simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Area 3: the DRL agent sets the IRS reflective coefficients (NoisyNet-SAC), jointly with bits per semantic symbol and subchannel assignment (NoisyNet-Dueling DQN); the transmit beamformer is not part of the action (p. 8). The semantic codec (VQ-VAE) is pre-trained and fine-tuned but the graded function is the IRS configuration. q3: the non-learned baselines are the AO Traditional Method [17] and the no-IRS scheme, the earlier learned baseline is the conventional HDRL [16], compared on reward, semantic security and S-SSE (Figs. 5, 7, 8); the ablations (CSO-SS, fixed layer selection, HDRL-DS without noise) are not counted. q4 rests on measured CPU time only; the paper gives no complexity order (p. 13). The figure legends cite the AO method as [19] and [18] while the text cites [17].
